stories.title: WVU leads a $321 million energy and AI engine, with up to $160 million from NSF.
stories.html: The Resilient Energy Technology and Infrastructure Consortium, led by WVU with the University of Pittsburgh, Carnegie Mellon, and more than 60 regional partners, will receive up to $160 million from the National Science Foundation over ten years, plus $161 million from industry, workforce, philanthropy, state government, and community partners. WVU's release says the consortium will develop hardware, software, and AI technologies to help secure the nation's energy supply and strengthen the grid. It says the funding is projected to generate 21,000 jobs, 150 startups, and more than $1 billion in economic growth for the region. Those are projections, not results.

stories.title: WVU researchers are building AI into field sensors.
stories.html: With an NSF Early-Concept Grant for Exploratory Research, biologist Steve Kannenberg and postdoctoral researcher Jie Hu are building AI and very small on-site computers into environmental monitoring sensors, so scientists could see how ecosystems respond to droughts and wildfires in near real time instead of waiting months or years. The project also includes a plain-language AI chatbot for the data. The researchers plan to test the approach at sites in Colorado and Massachusetts.

stories.title: WVU launches M.S. in Artificial Intelligence.
stories.html: A fully online graduate program from the Statler College's Lane Department of Computer Science and Electrical Engineering, covering machine learning, cybersecurity, intelligent systems, and energy applications. Enrollment opened Spring 2026, alongside companion M.S. tracks in Applied AI & Data Analytics and AI Marketing.

stories.title: WVU launches Strategic Compass seed innovation fund.
stories.html: President Benson unveiled seed funding to turn ideas into action across education, discovery, health, and service, with initial investors sought through the Day of Giving on March 25, 2026.

stories.title: 1Mby1M Virtual Accelerator and AI Mentor launches for WV.
stories.html: West Virginia entrepreneurs get access to an equity-free accelerator with AI-guided mentorship, global case studies, and frameworks for bootstrapping and scaling tech startups without leaving the state.

stories.title: Anurag Srivastava leads WVU cyber-power research.
stories.html: The Power Chair Professor in the Lane Department of Computer Science and Electrical Engineering works across power systems, cybersecurity, and AI, backed by more than $66 million from DOE, NSF, DARPA, and industry partners.
stories.dnote: Faculty profile page; no publication date.

stories.title: Data Driven WV pairs students with real-world AI work.
stories.html: Run out of the John Chambers College of Business and Economics under executive director Joshua Meadows, the center connects West Virginia organizations with student and faculty teams on data analytics, AI, and broadband deployment projects.
stories.dnote: Center page; no publication date shown.

stories.title: WVU BOG approves new AI and Smart Systems tracks.
stories.html: Undergraduate concentrations in AI/Computational Data Science and Cyber-Physical Systems, plus interdisciplinary programs pairing computer science with mechanical engineering.

stories.title: WVU F1Tenth team takes second nationally.
stories.html: Students built AI-powered self-driving scale cars and placed second at the IEEE international competition, an experiential learning initiative within the Lane Department.

stories.title: WVU AI Symposium 2025.
stories.html: Researchers presented work on dermatological AI analysis, anti-cancer peptide design, autonomous manufacturing algorithms, and broadband equity mapping for rural Appalachia.

stories.title: GATC Health expands AI drug discovery.
stories.html: The biotech firm uses its proprietary AI platform to develop non-opioid, non-habit-forming treatments for addiction, backed by a $5M West Virginia investment.

stories.title: NOAA announced a supercomputer, Rhea, for its Fairmont computing center.
stories.html: In September 2024 NOAA announced a $99 million investment in Rhea, a high-performance computer for its Environmental Security Computing Center in Fairmont. NOAA said it will strengthen the agency's AI and machine learning work on weather, ocean, and climate forecasting. The money comes from the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law and the Inflation Reduction Act. This entry reports the announcement. NOAA's computing-systems page lists Hera, Ursa, and Mercury at Fairmont and does not mention Rhea, so we have not confirmed whether Rhea is installed or running.

stories.title: Foundation CEO: NOAA's Fairmont computing center is unlikely to feel federal layoffs.
stories.html: After new federal layoffs hit NOAA in February 2025, the president and CEO of the West Virginia High Technology Foundation, which developed the I-79 Technology Park, told WBOY he had not been made aware of any cuts at the NOAA facility there and would be surprised by any disruption, because the work is considered "mission critical." He said he does not speak for NOAA or the federal government. He also said the agency signed a new 20-year lease at the park in September 2024.

stories.title: NOAA's Rhea supercomputer comes online at NESCC Fairmont.
stories.html: General Dynamics IT delivered the $100M Rhea HPC at the NOAA Environmental Security Computing Center, adding roughly 30 petaflops of research capacity for next-generation weather and climate AI/ML modeling.

stories.title: NASA Katherine Johnson IV&V Facility.
stories.html: Over 275 employees in Fairmont provide independent software verification and validation for NASA's highest-profile missions, including human spaceflight and deep-space exploration programs.
stories.dnote: Facility profile; the page shows only an 'Updated' stamp, not a publication date.

stories.title: I-79 Technology Park and NOAA supercomputing.
stories.html: The site hosts three NOAA ground stations and a supercomputing center, with foundation plans to apply AI and supercomputing to the multi-billion-dollar commercial weather data market.

stories.title: Thunkable's AI pilot gets about 120 West Virginia students building apps.
stories.html: In a pilot run with the State of West Virginia and supported by the Rockefeller Foundation, about 120 high school students in Monongalia, Kanawha, and Berkeley counties built an estimated 80 mobile apps with Thunkable's no-code app builder and its AI tools, and four schools completed the curriculum. Thunkable reports that 44% of students said they were more interested in starting a business. These figures come from Thunkable's own press release, which the Rockefeller Foundation posted.

sources.label: Thunkable pilot release, Rockefeller Foundation, Sep 10, 2026

stories.title: West Virginia is building a statewide AI training model for teachers.
stories.html: The West Virginia Department of Education is developing a train-the-trainer approach to AI professional learning, designed for a state of 55 counties and thousands of educators. Regional specialists will support local leaders known as AI Mountaineers, who will help deliver the training in their counties and schools. The department's professional learning initiative is called PAINT, for Pedagogical AI for New Teaching, and the broader plan has three levels: Pioneer, Trailblazer, and Ridge Climber. The Southern Regional Education Board's account of a podcast conversation with the department's AI coordinator says the model is still being implemented and its long-term outcomes remain to be seen. State Superintendent Michele Blatt told a U.S. House committee in February 2026 that the department provides ongoing professional development focused on the science of teaching with AI integration, which it calls PAiNT. We found no count of teachers trained.

sources.label: State Superintendent's written testimony, U.S. House Education and Workforce Committee, Feb 24, 2026

stories.title: Secretary of State's AI-powered knowledge center wins an international award.
stories.html: The Secretary of State's office says its Internal Knowledge Center, which integrates knowledge management and artificial intelligence into a single employee experience, earned a 2026 Merit Award at the International Association of Commercial Administrators' annual conference. The office is a repeat winner of the association's awards.

stories.title: Southern WV Community & Technical College wins $1.8 million to bring AI across the college.
stories.html: The U.S. Department of Education's Fund for the Improvement of Postsecondary Education (FIPSE) program funded a four-year AI Readiness and Capacity Initiative at the college, to bring AI into academic programs and student services.

sources.label: Southern WV Community & Technical College, Jan 13, 2026

stories.title: Morrisey unveils a 20-year data center plan.
stories.html: The Responsible Data Center Development Plan (Aug 11, 2026) sets seven principles, puts Chris Morris's Data Economy Office in charge, and promises an advisory council on setbacks and noise. Critics say it leaves HB 2014's regulatory gaps in place.

stories.title: WV Digital Government Summit returns to Charleston.
stories.html: State and local government leaders, sponsors, and technology partners convene on October 29, 2026 to plan digital transformation, AI implementation, and cybersecurity strategy.

stories.title: Morrisey closes 2026 session: 12 vetoes, 10 bills unsigned.
stories.html: The Governor finished work on the 2026 regular session. Separately, HB 4983, which approves the data center certification rule and keeps petitions confidential, became law, while bills to restore local control died.

stories.title: HB 4983 clears House 78-16: data-center confidentiality.
stories.html: The bill lets the Morrisey administration withhold basic data-center project details from the public. Critics say it shields lawmakers from accountability on a major economic question.

stories.title: Legislature blocks local-control restoration bills.
stories.html: Lawmakers repeatedly blocked 2026-session efforts to return data-center siting authority to counties and municipalities, preserving HB 2014's preemption of local zoning.

stories.title: State AI Task Force ongoing oversight.
stories.html: Established under §5A-6-9 of WV Code, the task force assesses AI's impact on employment, government services, and economic development, with a January 2026 meeting on the public agenda.

stories.title: S.O.LO: WV's first government AI chatbot.
stories.html: The Secretary of State's office deployed an AI assistant to guide users through business filings and registrations, winning the 2025 IACA True Merit Award at the 48th Annual Conference for its business-registry implementation.

stories.title: WV named among 16 states for OpenAI's Stargate project.
stories.html: West Virginia is on OpenAI's shortlist for its $500 billion multi-campus AI infrastructure initiative, with the company actively scouting sites that meet power and water requirements.

stories.title: TechConnect WV: 20+ years of tech innovation.
stories.html: Based in South Charleston, TechConnect WV supports tech entrepreneurship statewide, connecting research, industry, and economic development from the earliest stages.

stories.title: WVIAIS: AI consulting for small business.
stories.html: West Virginia Integrated AI Solutions focuses on making AI affordable for small businesses across the state, with a specialty in data entry and administrative automation.

stories.title: Marshall's medical school builds AI into training and clinics.
stories.html: The Joan C. Edwards School of Medicine says it is integrating AI across education, with adaptive-learning platforms and AI-assisted case generation for students. It describes clinical tools including an AI system that detects polyps during colonoscopies and an AI documentation assistant, alongside bioinformatics and AI research, including its Translational Bioinformatics and AI Innovations Lab.

sources.label: Marshall School of Medicine, "AI & Medicine," Mar 19, 2026

stories.title: Marshall plans an AI simulation pilot for counseling training.
stories.html: In January 2026 Marshall announced that its Department of Counseling had signed an agreement with Soma Lab Inc. (SimCare AI), a for-profit maker of AI-driven clinical simulation software, for design, a pilot program, and evaluation. Marshall said it would receive early access to the software beginning that spring, contribute faculty expertise, help gather user feedback, take part in pilot testing, and seek grant funding for a wider rollout. The announcement names no funding, and we have not confirmed the pilot's current status.

stories.title: Marshall builds a $45 million cybersecurity institute.
stories.html: Neighborgall Construction is building the $45 million, roughly 72,000-square-foot Institute for Cyber Security in Huntington, due to open in August 2027. It will hold advanced cyber ranges, digital forensics labs, unmanned-systems research space, and operational-technology environments. WSAZ reported in August 2026 that cyber defense work is already under way at several campus locations, and that Intuit launched a security operations center on campus in June.

sources.label: Marshall Institute for Cyber Security, "ICS Building Updates"

stories.title: Quality Insights gifts $1.2M to Marshall iCenter.
stories.html: The funding pays for a full-time gener8tor program manager in Huntington, two gBETA accelerator cohorts per year for three years, and a new gALPHA ideation cohort for early-stage startup testing.

stories.title: Marshall University's AI governance.
stories.html: Marshall's Presidential Task Force on AI, formed in 2023, now continues as an AI Steering Committee with AI Enablement and Academic AI Integration sub-committees. Students, faculty, and staff get Coursera's Career Academy, with 6,000+ courses.

stories.title: IDEA District and the $45M Institute for Cyber Security.
stories.html: Marshall's Innovation District takes shape west of campus with a state-funded cybersecurity facility under construction, anchored alongside the Brad D. Smith Center for Business and Innovation. The Institute opens in summer 2027.

stories.title: Marshall and Intuit forge a strategic partnership.
stories.html: The collaboration creates a hiring pipeline for tech, cybersecurity, and AI jobs, plus a prosperity hub in the Innovation District for financial education and hands-on AI, tax, and bookkeeping training.

stories.title: Marshall's first gBETA cohort.
stories.html: Five startups were chosen for the inaugural gBETA cohort at Marshall's iCenter: FarmerzTool Technology, get2there, Monarch Learning Labs, Quest R&D, and Stitch AI, with support from Huntington National Bank.

stories.title: Generation WV AI workforce panel.
stories.html: Josh Spence, chair of the WV Task Force on Artificial Intelligence and CIO at Alpha Innovations, told the July 2025 panel: "AI is the priority." On infrastructure: "Broadband is not a nice-to-have. It is a must-have."

stories.title: Helsing plans a $50 million AI-enabled drone factory in Martinsburg.
stories.html: The Governor announced on July 13, 2026 that the German defense company Helsing will invest an initial $50 million in Berkeley County to make its HX-2 AI-enabled strike drone. The Governor's office says the plant will create at least 60 full-time jobs averaging $125,000 a year. Metro News reports that Helsing's U.S. general manager said the plant would produce 2,000 drones a month. The state developed a customized workforce training program with West Virginia Advance and Blue Ridge Community and Technical College. This is defense manufacturing, and the jobs and production figures are announced plans, not results.

stories.title: One year post-HB 2014: transparency and grid-cost concerns surface.
stories.html: Ratepayer advocates and Appalachian Power warn that the law's microgrid backup provisions could raise customer bills, while environmental groups flag gaps in air-quality oversight for fast-tracked sites.

stories.title: Residents call for protections as data-center buildout accelerates.
stories.html: Host communities in Berkeley, Tucker, and Mason counties are organizing for health, noise, and grid-impact protections, citing "empty promises" on community benefit and accountability.

stories.title: $4 billion Penzance data center announced.
stories.html: Governor Morrisey unveiled WV's first High Impact Intelligence Center: a 548-acre, roughly 1.9 million sq ft campus in the Falling Waters District with 600 MW of critical IT capacity. No state funding was used.

stories.title: Nscale takes over Monarch; Anthropic signs on.
stories.html: UK-based Nscale bought Fidelis-affiliated American Intelligence & Power Corp. (AIPCorp) in March 2026 and now runs the Mason County Monarch Compute Campus. The phase-one 2.16 GW gas microgrid is under DEP air review, and Anthropic agreed to pay up to approximately $44.6B for GPU capacity there (Nscale S-1). See Project Watch.

stories.title: HB 2014: Certified Microgrid Program.
stories.html: Effective July 2025, the law set up WV's microgrid certification framework and streamlined permitting for data centers, positioning the state to compete with Northern Virginia's Data Center Alley.

stories.title: Microgrid revenue reinvestment.
stories.html: Under HB 2014, data center revenue flows 50% to a Personal Income Tax Reduction Fund, 30% to the host county, 10% to all counties per capita, and 5% each to the Electric Grid Stabilization and Security Fund and the Economic Enhancement Grant Program.

stories.title: Berkeley County asks the AG how HB 2014 preemption works. The AG declines.
stories.html: County officials sent a 10-page request about stormwater MS4 duties and public service districts around the Penzance site. AG J.B. McCuskey declined on Oct 9, citing the pending Barks lawsuit in Ohio County.

stories.title: PowerFlo Solutions plans a $20 million manufacturing site in Williamstown.
stories.html: PowerFlo Solutions, led by West Virginia native Jim Vuksic, will invest $20 million to establish advanced manufacturing operations in the 240,000-square-foot former Hino plant in Williamstown, the Governor's office announced. The Governor's release says the project will create between 120 and 200 full-time jobs, and Metro News reports at least 120. Metro News says the company, which is based in Marietta, Ohio, designs and builds electrical equipment for data centers and AI, such as power distribution units, static transfer switches, dry-type transformers, and custom control panels. The state made an adjacent 11-acre parcel available for expansion. The job figures are announced plans, not results.

stories.title: WVU-P Innovation and Technology Center opens.
stories.html: WVU-P invested nearly $35 million to turn the former Ohio Valley University campus in Vienna into its Innovation and Technology Center. Classes began in August 2025 with 159 students, including hands-on cybersecurity and networking work.

stories.title: WV Digital Government Summit, Wheeling participation.
stories.html: Wheeling leaders are slated to join state and local officials at the October 29, 2026 statewide summit in Charleston to plan digital transformation, AI implementation, and cybersecurity strategy.

stories.title: Emerging IT-enabled services hub.
stories.html: Niche IT and tech startups are forming in Wheeling, with founders gaining access to the 1Mby1M equity-free virtual accelerator and AI Mentor for market validation and growth.

stories.title: Form Energy lands $1B Google deal.
stories.html: Weirton's iron-air battery factory will produce the world's largest battery system (300MW / 30GWh, 100-hour duration) to power a Google data center in Minnesota. First commercial deployment for a data center.

stories.title: Weirton plant targets 500 MW a year by 2028.
stories.html: Form Energy's Weirton factory, which will build the iron-air batteries for the Google and Xcel Energy project, is expected to reach 500 MW of annual production capacity by 2028.

stories.title: State guidance brings AI into classrooms.
stories.html: A Mercer County Schools technology integration specialist says teachers work from the WV Department of Education's AI guidance as schools adopt AI tools for lesson planning and instruction.

stories.title: Mercer County trains teachers on AI.
stories.html: Mercer County Public Schools teachers and faculty trained on AI tools at the district's back-to-school assembly.

stories.title: WVU Tech hosts Governor's Computer Science Institute.
stories.html: The residential summer program teaches AI, coding, and drone programming to West Virginia high schoolers. Three-year commitment starts summer 2026 on the Beckley campus.

stories.title: WVU Tech President joins national AI Leadership Council.
stories.html: President T. Ramon Stuart was appointed to Ruffalo Noel Levitz's AI Leadership Council, shaping AI strategy in higher education and positioning WVU Tech as a pipeline for AI professionals.

stories.title: The FBI's biometrics center in Clarksburg marks ten years.
stories.html: The FBI's biometrics center opened in 2015 on the Criminal Justice Information Services Division campus in Clarksburg, a 360,000-square-foot facility. The FBI's anniversary story is mostly about fingerprint and iris systems. It says the algorithms for fingerprints, latent prints, face, and iris have each been upgraded, and it quotes an FBI assistant director crediting artificial intelligence for the accuracy of the fingerprint and iris algorithms.

stories.title: TekSynap acquires JBA, strengthening FBI tech support.
stories.html: The acquisition expands TekSynap's IT, cloud, and cyber support for FBI programs, including the CJIS Division in Clarksburg.

stories.title: FBI CJIS Division in Clarksburg.
stories.html: The secure 986-acre campus has about 3,500 employees and contractors, most in CJIS Main and the Biometric Technology Center.
stories.dnote: FBI division profile; no publication date (the page blocks automated readers).

stories.title: Ridgeline appeals tossed on jurisdiction; groups vow to refile.
stories.html: The Air Quality Board upheld Fundamental Data's permit in February. On Aug 26 the Intermediate Court of Appeals dismissed the appeals by Tucker United, the WV Highlands Conservancy, and the Sierra Club on jurisdictional grounds, not the merits. NPR covered the fight nationally on Oct 31.

stories.title: Harvard study projects $19M to $35M in health damages.
stories.html: A report via the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health's Dominici lab estimates health-related damages if the expected Ridgeline operation runs as permitted.

stories.title: Groups appeal for blacked-out Ridgeline permit data.
stories.html: Citizen groups say emissions data and design details are blacked out in Fundamental Data's air permit application, and appealed to get the information released.
